title: Caricatures of Irencillia
heading: Culture and Traditions
requires: Residence at Irencillia (House Merinita domus magna)
summary: Every long-term magus resident at Irencillia gains a faerie double, a caricature raised from the servant-folk, whose Faerie Might can grow with the magus's status and which may become an Arcane Connection to its human. Residents are treated as having the Faerie Friend Flaw for the duration of their stay.
quotes: In game terms, every long-term resident of Irencillia gains the Faerie Friend Flaw for the duration of his or her visit.

title: Irencillia: Shifting Appearance and Patchy Faerie Aura
heading: Setting and Physical Description
summary: Faerie glamour makes the covenant look and feel different to each visitor, with sancta and communal areas settling into a firm consensus reality. Its Faerie aura varies from place to place, with the strongest patches (some inside regiones) holding the magi's sancta.
quotes: The Faerie aura of Irencillia is highly patchy.
All areas within the boundary wall have an aura of at least 1

title: Mount Radhost Ritual and Corpus Vis
heading: Mount Radhost
summary: The summit temple holds a strong Magic aura, and the yearly solstice festival to Radegast, fuelled by human sacrifice, lets the Roznov magi harvest large amounts of vis, including Corpus vis from the blood.
quotes: It has a Magic aura of 6.
The blood of the sacrifices is harvested for Corpus vis.

title: Radegast
heading: Radegast
summary: Describes the pagan Slavic god Radegast and the Virtues and Flaw his favored followers tend to display, useful when building his devotees as characters.
quotes: Those he favors often display the Inspirational and Great Presence Virtues, as well as the Overconfident Flaw.
related: Between the Devil and the Deep Blue Sea (Chapter 11)

title: Establishing Your Covenant: Four Starting Options
heading: Establishing Your Covenant
summary: Sets out four ways a group of Rhine magi can begin a saga: founding a new covenant, establishing a chapter house, settling at an existing covenant, or travelling between covenants as peregrinatores. Each option carries different approval requirements, resources and independence.
quotes: Any covenant with sufficient resources might support chapters
related: Chapter 3: The Rhine Tribunal, On the Founding of Covenants

title: Chapter Houses
heading: ESTABLISHING A CHAPTER HOUSE
summary: A chapter house lets a covenant with enough resources support additional sites. Chapters need no Tribunal approval and receive resources from the motherhouse, but are bound by the parent covenant's charter.
quotes: Chapters are not new covenants, therefore they do not require the approval of Tribunal; also, the motherhouse will provide resources for its foundation.

title: Peregrinatores: Travelling Between Covenants
heading: TRAVEL FROM COVENANT TO COVENANT
summary: The Rhine Tribunal's tradition of hospitality lets wandering magi guest at other covenants without a permanent home of their own.
quotes: traditions of hospitality for wandering magi
related: Chapter 3: The Rhine Tribunal, Upon Being a Rhine Magus

title: The Order of Odin: Norse Wizard Options
heading: The Order of Odin
requires: Storyguide decision: existence of Norse wizards
summary: Leaves it to the storyguide to decide whether Norse wizards exist and how organized they are, from a Norse equivalent of the Order of Hermes to scattered weak hedge magicians, and lists the kinds of magic Norse legends attribute to them.
quotes: No single Norse magician should be capable of doing all these things.

title: Radegast and Gymir: Disguised Infernal Auras
heading: Between the Devil and the Deep Blue Sea
summary: Describes two rival demon princes, how heavily the Order may be infiltrated, and Radegast's ability to disguise Infernal power so that his sites register as Magic or Faerie auras.
quotes: he is able to disguise his infernal power as magic or faerie power

title: Fenistal: A Single-Level Magic Regio
heading: Fenistal
summary: The exsules' hidden base lies in the upper level of a Magic regio from which all intermediate levels have been removed by powerful magic, making it very hard to reach.
quotes: with a Magic aura of 8

title: The Exsules: A Renegade Hermetic Tradition
heading: The Exsules
requires: Tradition: Exsules of Fenistal (outcast House Merinita)
summary: Profiles the isolated Hermetic exiles outside the Order, listing the Flaws they all share from their isolation and imperfect Parma Magica, the Virtues common among them, and how their magic should feel alien to Hermetic magi.
quotes: all suffer the Weird Magic Flaw due to their isolation from the Order
all have inherited the Flawed Parma Magica Flaw
related: Chapter 4: The Forest (Paths through the Forest)

title: Saga Magi: Characters and Starting Resources
heading: Magi
summary: Guidance for building the player magi for the Curse of the Rhine Gorge saga: backgrounds, optional Gild Trained for Rhine-apprenticed magi, and a spread of starting resources such as shield grogs and money, with Fengheld magi favored.
quotes: the Minor Virtue (Gild) Trained
which allows them to start with a personal shield grog and a reasonable sum of money
related: Chapter 3: Tribunal History and Customs, Upon Being a Rhine Magus

title: Saga Grogs and Shield Grogs
heading: Grogs
summary: Explains that grogs are less central than magi, need not be taken at the very start, and may be recruited or donated as a founding gift; a shield grog should be played by someone other than the magus's player.
quotes: A grog who is assigned to be the shield grog of a particular magus should be played by someone other than the player of that magus.

title: Saga Start: A Gentle Introduction
heading: A GENTLE INTRODUCTION
summary: An easier saga start in which an existing friendly covenant supplies labs, books, grogs, vis or money while the young magi explore before settling.

title: Saga Start: In at the Deep End
heading: IN AT THE DEEP END
summary: A harder saga start in which the magi leave Durenmar lightly equipped with scant resources and must found the covenant from the ground up.

title: Mouse Swarm Attacks (Mäuseturm)
heading: The Mice of the Mäuseturm
summary: A swarm of demonic mice automatically damages victims each round according to the protection they wear, with no attack roll, and is driven off when over half the mice are killed. Includes how area spells and Brawl attacks affect a swarm and why the swarm regenerates in an Infernal aura.
quotes: No attack roll is required for the mice

title: Loreley: Treacherous River Stretch
heading: Loreley
summary: The narrowest stretch of the Rhine Gorge is dangerous to boats even without the siren, with a Boating roll needed by crews who have not learned the positions of the rocks, and the cliff has a Faerie aura.
quotes: Ease Factor 9 for those who have not learned the positions of the rocks

title: The Rhine Faerie Courts: Seasonal Dominion
heading: The Faerie Courts
summary: Describes the rival Seelie and Unseelie faerie courts on either side of the Rhine, when and where each can be found, how they alternate dominion through the year, and how they can become contested vis sources. Offers the Courts of the Seasons as an alternative.
quotes: Dark Summer holds dominion over Bright Winter from Walpurgis Night until All Hallows Eve, and vice versa.
related: Chapter 4: The Forest (Courts of the Seasons)

title: Seeking Tribunal Approval for a New Covenant
heading: Seeking Tribunal Approval
summary: Rhine law requires a prospective covenant to be sponsored by one magus from every other covenant, which usually means trading promises, favors and debts; the sponsorship of a single magus is enough from each covenant.
quotes: a prospective covenant must be sponsored by one magus from every other covenant in the Tribunal
related: Chapter 3: Tribunal History and Customs, On the Founding of Covenants

title: The Receiving of Gifts
heading: THE RECEIVING OF GIFTS
summary: Each sponsor gives the new covenant a gift whose value reflects that covenant's greatness and attitude, such as books, magic items, valuables or grogs, delivered immediately or in later seasons.

title: Companions for the Saga
heading: Companions
summary: Suggests companion character types that magi may befriend as the covenant settles in, and advises making a player's companion dissimilar to their magus.
quotes: these two characters should ideally be dissimilar

title: Imperial Toll Levels
heading: IMPERIAL TOLL LEVELS
summary: A table of the emperor's set toll per vessel type, the daily income a toll station can expect from passing traffic, and the need for armed enforcement against rivals and toll-runners.
quotes: Small rowboat (5 persons or less) — 1d
Large ship (two or more masts) — 12d
providing a daily income of 10 schillings or more

title: By Land or by River? (Merchant Route Choice)
heading: BY LAND OR BY RIVER?
summary: Explains how merchants weigh shipwreck risk against overland banditry and tolls when choosing between river transport and portage, including the common portage bypass of the Bingen Hole.

title: Languages in Germany and Mutual Intelligibility
heading: LANGUAGES IN GERMANY
summary: Lists the Living Languages of Germany with their dialect specialties and gives penalties applied when speakers of related languages or dialects try to understand each other, with a worked example.
quotes: **Same language, different dialects:** –1 penalty to both speakers
**High German vs Low German:** –2 penalty to both speakers
**High German vs East Norse or English:** –4 penalty to both speakers
